It sounds like you're experiencing issues with offset pagination against a changing collection. This can cause records to be skipped or duplicated. We recommend using cursor pagination instead, which is designed to handle changing data. To switch to cursor pagination, pass the next_cursor value from each response as the cursor parameter of the following request, and stop when it is null. [DOC-API-002]

We've identified that the issue may be related to database connection pool exhaustion. This can occur when the pool size multiplied by the instance count exceeds the database connection limit. You can check the database plan comparison page to see the connection limit. Additionally, it's possible that connections are not being returned to the pool after use, or long-running transactions are holding connections open. Please review the resolution steps in [DOC-PERF-003] for more information on how to diagnose and resolve this issue.

The issue you're experiencing with signature verification failing on your webhook endpoint is likely due to the signature being computed over a parsed body rather than the raw bytes [DOC-API-003]. To resolve this, compute the signature over the raw request body before any parsing. Re-serialising JSON changes the bytes and invalidates the signature [DOC-API-003].

This means moving any data read from a file on disk to environment variables or secrets. This will ensure that your data is preserved and can be accessed after the migration. [DOC-ONB-002][DOC-ONB-001]
